gen-dm-serif-text-fs-spline-sans: Spline Sans keeps every stroke at the same measured thickness, with wide gaps where curves meet stems. And DM Serif Text sits above it with heavy stems and hairline arms, so the page feels like a bookish headline over a friendly, uniform line.
gen-dm-serif-text-fs-supreme: Supreme runs a tall, heavy-looking strip of crisp lowercase, its letters held open rather than curled shut. Supreme's sturdy, steady texture is the pair's real strength, standing firm under DM Serif Text and its sharp thick-thin drama.
gen-dm-serif-text-manrope: Manrope leaves a bright gap at the mouth of every curve and barely steps down from capital to lowercase. Manrope's smooth single-width line gives DM Serif Text, with its moderate lowercase height and heavy stems, a tidy sans-serif partner underneath.
gen-dm-serif-text-outfit: Ink-heavy and feather-light, then wire-smooth. DM Serif Text does its best work with fat stems and hairline arms that feel editorial, while Outfit does its best with curves that stop short of closing, drawn in one constant line.
gen-dm-serif-text-satoshi: Glowing, almost neon, describes the body here: every stroke cut to one width. Satoshi lifts its lowercase high and keeps the e wide open, a bright counterweight to the thick stems of DM Serif Text.
gen-dm-serif-text-switzer: Scratchy hairlines meet wire-straight tubes. DM Serif Text is best at bold uprights with horizontals thin as scratches, while Switzer is best at a pen line that holds one width, with c tips that never creep toward touching.
gen-dm-serif-text-work-sans: Work Sans holds a tube-like, constant-width stroke under a mean line set high, with c tips that stay apart. But DM Serif Text swells boldly and thins sharply above it, sitting lower in the lowercase and giving the page a lively tension.
gen-fraunces-fs-amulya: A slight pinch where curves meet straight stems marks Fraunces, which is dignified and bookish with generous openings on every curve. Amulya does its best work in the sans role, keeping its curve gaps just as generous and staying modern and low in contrast.
gen-fraunces-fs-epilogue: Approachable is the word for Epilogue's curvy, tall-bodied lowercase, though that comes second here. Fraunces does its best with mild thicks and a bookish dignity, while Epilogue does its best with a wire-like monoline skeleton and stubby ascender tips.
gen-fraunces-fs-plein: A thickness shift you feel more than see runs through Fraunces, and its curves open generously at every terminal. And Plein gives the pair its best quality: a clear channel into each round letter, reliable and clean under that bookish dignity.
